title: Prime multipliers of order ten: norm spectra, local charts, and selective lifting
summary: Write P(N) for the assertion that every principal minor of the Fourier matrix of order N is nonzero. The square-free principal-minor conjecture was previously known for a few uniform small-multiplier families, including several families with two prime factors; broader higher-factor results were non-uniform, apart from isolated exact verifications. We prove a near-complete prime-multiplier theorem for the composite base 10: P(10p) holds for every prime p \notin {2,5,11}.
